name: Avis Budget Group, Inc.
description: Avis Budget Group operates car and truck rental businesses under the Avis, Budget, and Zipcar brands in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia, and Australia. The company is highly capital-intensive, financing large vehicle fleets, and has been under significant financial pressure since the pandemic-era peak in used car valuations began to unwind. As of Q1 2026 it carries approximately $24 billion in total obligations and negative stockholders' equity of roughly $3.4 billion.

notable_events.event: Historic short squeeze: shares rallied from ~$100 to $713.97 (April 21) driven by a constrained free float (~10M shares) and short interest exceeding 80% of tradeable shares, then collapsed more than 75% within days as covering momentum exhausted.

Q1 2026 earnings: Revenue $2.53B (+4% YoY, beat), EPS -$8.01 (missed consensus -$7.14 by $0.87), Adjusted EBITDA -$113M (worsened YoY). Stock fell further on the miss despite operational improvements.
Full-year 2025 revenue $11.65B (-1.16% YoY), net loss $889M. Q4 2025 included a $518M non-cash EV fleet impairment charge.

recent: In April 2026 Avis was the subject of a historic short squeeze: shares rallied from roughly $100 to $713.97 on April 21 — driven by a constrained free float (~10 million shares) and short interest exceeding 80% of tradeable shares — then collapsed more than 75% within days as covering momentum exhausted. Q1 2026 earnings on April 29 reported revenue of $2.53 billion (+4% YoY, beat) but EPS of -$8.01 (missing the -$7.14 consensus by $0.87) and Adjusted EBITDA of -$113 million (worsened YoY); the stock fell further on the miss despite operational improvements. Full-year 2025 revenue was $11.65 billion (-1.16% YoY) with a $889 million net loss, including a $518 million non-cash EV fleet impairment charge in Q4 2025.
